recommendation: Keep the commit as-is. It preserves the original FHIR-17537 decision, fixes only directly adjacent source drift in the canonical target list, and does not broaden canonical(Any) beyond resources with canonical URLs.
issue_request: FHIR-17537 was Published/Persuasive for STU3 and asked the specification to clarify that canonical(Any) means any resource with a canonical URL, with the in-scope resources explicitly listed.
initial_application: SVN revision 14506, represented by git commit a4e7ed6b160c641d9bca3d6ebd0e45afbc4eac8c, added the canonical(Any) target restriction to source/references.html. Follow-up commits fd55abe2059b0cde64394016922d12259d049a0b and 9c858ce3d24372d302e90f0440fa167b199ed845 refined the wording and datatype-table link to the canonical list.
additional_context: The current datatype page links canonical to references.html#canonical-list as resources with a url property, and the references page still says canonical(Any) references SHALL only reference those canonical-resource types. Later FHIR-30696 source work linked the list to CanonicalResource. A 2025 QA edit inserted an incomplete Additional Resources sentence in the same section, immediately before the canonical(Any) rule.
reconciliation: Changed source/references.html to complete that sentence as: 'In addition, some types of Additional Resources also have canonical URLs.' No other source behavior or target-scope rule was changed.
source_changes: source/references.html: completed the Additional Resources sentence in the Canonical Resources section before the existing canonical(Any) SHALL restriction.

related_jiras.note: Updated canonical resource list wording and supports retaining the list as the scope anchor for canonical(Any); no separate decision was needed.
Corrected typo fallout in the canonical datatype description after the original FHIR-17537 wording; no current source change was needed for that issue.
